memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Whenever the ark set out, Moses said, "Rise up, Lord! May your enemies be scattered; may your foes flee before you." Whenever it came to rest, he said, "Return, Lord, to the countless thousands of Israel." - Num 10:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the ark set out each day, Moses prayed, "Rise up, Lord!" And when it came to rest, he prayed, "Return, Lord." Every stage of the journey was wrapped in prayer. Moses began each movement by calling on God to go before them and scatter their enemies, and he ended each stage by asking God's presence to settle among them again.

What a picture of a life soaked in prayer. Moses did not treat God's presence as a lucky charm to be carried along; he actively called on the Lord at every step. When it was time to move, he prayed for God to lead and to overcome all opposition. When it was time to rest, he prayed for God's nearness among the people.

This teaches us to bracket our days and our journeys with prayer. As we set out — into a new day, a new task, a new challenge — we can pray, "Rise up, Lord; go before me." And as we come to rest — at the end of the day, the end of a season — we can pray, "Return, Lord; dwell with us."

Moses' confidence was that God's cause would triumph and His enemies would scatter. That confidence is fulfilled in Christ, who has triumphed over every enemy through the cross (Col 2:15), and who will one day put all enemies under His feet (1 Cor 15:25).

As this chapter ends, let Moses' prayers become ours. In our going out and our coming in, may we call upon the Lord — asking Him to lead us forward and to dwell among us. He rises up for His people, and He returns to make His home with them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you bracket your days and journeys with prayer?
- What would it mean to pray "Rise up, Lord" as you set out?
- How does Christ's victory give you confidence as you follow God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Rise up, O Lord, and go before me; scatter all that opposes Your purposes in my life. And return, Lord, to dwell near me and give me rest. In Jesus' name, Amen.
